concepts.title: Tenali Rama's Wit Wins Hearts
concepts.section: The Wit that Won Hearts, Let us read
concepts.definition: Tenali Ramakrishna, the witty poet of Krishnadeva Raya's court, uses humour instead of argument; a plate of paddy seeds and a joke about yawning melt the king's anger and reunite him with Queen Thirumalambal.
concepts.key_idea: Wit works where lectures fail: laughter opens the mind that pride had closed.
concepts.textbook_ref: hepr101.txt, The Wit that Won Hearts, Let us read

solution_steps.explain: Retell the main happenings in one or two sentences.
Point to the moment of change, realisation or sacrifice.
Say the message of the text in one sentence of your own.

concepts.title: Pride and Apology: The Royal Quarrel
concepts.section: The Wit that Won Hearts, Let us think and reflect
concepts.definition: A small misunderstanding grows when pride blinds the king; harmony returns only when he admits that he overreacted, showing that a sincere apology can end a long silence.
concepts.key_idea: Pride prolongs quarrels; admitting fault, as the king does, needs maturity and self-awareness.
concepts.textbook_ref: hepr101.txt, The Wit that Won Hearts, Let us think and reflect

solution_steps.explain: Note the tiny trigger, a yawn during a poem, that began the quarrel.
Describe the sadness the quarrel spreads through the palace.
Trace the apology that restores the bond and the joy of the court.

concepts.title: A Strategy of Indirect Teaching
concepts.section: The Wit that Won Hearts, Let us read
concepts.definition: Tenali Rama asks for time and plans his move; he raises the paddy seed matter in open court, lets the courtiers laugh first, and leads the king to the truth about yawning without ever mentioning the quarrel.
concepts.key_idea: Indirect teaching protects dignity: the learner discovers the lesson himself, so it is accepted gladly.
concepts.textbook_ref: hepr101.txt, The Wit that Won Hearts, Let us read
question_patterns: why does tenali rama ask for time before helping the queen

what makes the king realise that yawning is natural

solution_steps.explain: Say what Rama wants: the king must see his own unfairness.
Trace each step, from the seed claim to the yawn question.
Explain why the indirect way succeeds where direct advice would fail.

concepts.title: Word Meanings: Distraught, Insurmountable and Sceptical
concepts.section: The Wit that Won Hearts, Let us learn
concepts.definition: Court-tale words take meaning from context: distraught means extremely sad, insurmountable means undefeatable, sceptical means doubtful, and orchestrated means arranged carefully.
concepts.key_idea: Feelings words like distraught and forlorn paint the silent palace before Rama's plan works.
concepts.textbook_ref: hepr101.txt, The Wit that Won Hearts, Let us learn

solution_steps.explain: Find the sentence where the new word appears.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Why does Tenali Rama introduce the paddy seeds in the full court instead of speaking to the king alone?

solution_template.explain: A private lecture on yawning would wound the king's pride all over again.
Before the whole court, the yawning joke becomes public laughter, letting the king laugh at himself and change without being shamed.

worked_examples.question_pattern: What does the queen's reply to the apology reveal about her?

solution_template.explain: She offers to leave the quarrel behind and asks to hear the poem.
Her readiness to forgive and her wish to listen show grace and affection.
